PROOF-1.case: the install lines of the README and of step 1 of the getting-started page; the proof says they are the same lines; the changed guide's first line reads `cd my-app` where the README reads `cd my-project`

explanation: PROOF-1: the test reads the install lines of both pages, compares the two lists whole, and compares the marketplace address of each page with a constant, so it observes both things the proof names.
PROOF-1: the helpers that pick the lines out of each page are not shown, so the test catches a difference in the `cd` line only if they keep every line of the block and not just the `claude` lines.
PROOF-1: the expected address comes from the constant `ADDRESS`, whose value is not shown; the test checks the proof's `https://github.com/rlabarca/purlin.git` only if the constant holds that text.
PROOF-1: the last two assertions check that a block under another heading gives no lines and that a one-word difference is unequal, which guard the helpers and not the proof's case.
Findings: none were made by the spot tests, and nothing in the test's own lines is a check that cannot fail.

PROOF-2.case: the install commands of the getting-started page run in an empty project; the proof says `purlin@purlin` is installed and enabled for that project; the changed page installs it at user scope, so it is not installed for that project

explanation: PROOF-2: the test takes the `installed` fixture, reads the `purlin` row and asserts it is enabled, at project scope and at the test's own project path, so an install at another scope or in another project fails it wherever the fixture runs that command.
PROOF-2: the test then runs `claude plugin list` in the project and asserts the output holds `purlin@purlin` and `enabled`, which is the observation the proof names.

PROOF-2: the fixture that reads the pages and runs their commands is not shown, so the test's own lines do not say which page's commands are run; a command changed on a page the fixture does not read would still pass.

PROOF-2: the word `enabled` is looked for anywhere in the listing, not on the `purlin@purlin` line, so the listing check alone would pass on another plugin's `enabled`; the row assertions above it cover that.
Findings: the spot tests found nothing, and the test holds failable assertions on the values the proof names.

PROOF-3.case: the install of PROOF-2 from this checkout; the proof says the folder the installed plugin reads its skills from holds a SKILL.md for each folder under skills/, byte for byte; the changed manifest points the plugin at docs, which holds no SKILL.md

explanation: PROOF-3: the test finds the skills folder through the installed plugin's own manifest, with `skills` as the default, and checks that it is a real folder inside the installed plugin.
PROOF-3: the test compares the set of folders holding a `SKILL.md` there with the checkout's skill folders, so a missing or an extra skill fails it.
PROOF-3: the test reads each installed `SKILL.md` and the checkout's as bytes and compares them whole, which is the "same bytes" the proof names.
PROOF-3: the list of expected names comes from a helper that is not shown, and the test only guards it with a floor of 9, so the check is as complete as that helper's listing of `skills/`.
PROOF-3: the spot tests found nothing, and the test asserts the proof's case and its result, so the planted change is the plain one.
